newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes plunge late on products, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes plunge late on products, weather.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices plunged late Friday in response to lower refined-product prices and bearish weather forecasts for the coming week, traders said.
On contract-expiry day for products, both gasoline and heating oil were undermined by profit-taking on the March contract, dragging down crude with them, traders said.
Compounding the downtrend are expectations for above-normal temperatures next week, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $24.10-20 a barrel, down 65 cents from late Thursday's cash market.
The March/April WTI spread was around 44 cents a barrel.
Grade differentials were relatively quiet, with many traders attending an industry-sponsored event in the Colorado Rockies.
WTI/Midland was talked weaker around 38-40 cents under WTI/Cushing, while Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was stronger, getting done late at WTI/Cushing plus 24/25/26/27 cents a barrel.
While the two grades often move in tandem when the market is tight, the current "sloshy" market climate has caused them to diverge, traders said.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done as high as $2.07 under WTI/Cushing, down four cents from Thursday's lowest trade.
Eugene Island was also weaker, trading at minus $2.10 a barrel, down 15 cents from Thursday.
